prompts.title: Recent form — kinetic typography to grouped count bars
prompts.prompt: Vertical 9:16 composition (1080x1920 reference) on GoatLab charcoal #101412. The lower quarter is permanently reserved for yellow subtitles — no type, bar or credit enters that band. EDITORIAL variant, kinetic typography with rhythmic emphasis: full-frame type stage. Spanish word 'RACHA' punches in at centre in warm white #edf0e6, tight tracking, then splits into two stacked name plates — 'Liverpool' above, 'Brighton' below — each underlined by a lime #c5ed74 rule that sweeps left to right on a spoken beat. Three beat slots rise in sequence, one Spanish word each: 'victorias', 'empates', 'derrotas', warm white on slate #8ca6bf hairline rules, landing on the drum hits with a 1.0 to 1.06 scale and settle. This variant carries no numerals, no axes and no sample claims; hierarchy is carried by size — team plates at three times the word size, one focal point at centre. Camera: slow three-depth push-in, then a lateral whip of half frame width to swap plates. Transition into the statistical block: the lime underline stretches to full frame width as a wipe mask. Exit: type plates slide upward through the wipe. STATISTICAL variant, grouped count bars: horizontal grouped bars on a shared zero baseline with one common scale in partidos, Liverpool row above Brighton row, lime #c5ed74 for Liverpool and slate #8ca6bf for Brighton, warm white value labels sitting at each bar end, Spanish axis label 'partidos' and warm white unit ticks. Resolved values animate as {{home.wins}} / {{away.wins}} for victorias, {{home.draws}} / {{away.draws}} for empates, {{home.losses}} / {{away.losses}} for derrotas. Bars grow from the baseline with a stagger, then the victorias pair takes emphasis via a lime glow pulse while camera holds a locked-off frame with a shallow push-in. Sample and source treatment: a footnote reading 'muestra' with {{home.n}} and {{away.n}} partidos plus source credit Bzzoiro, set in 22 px slate, pinned just above the subtitle band. Transition: bars retract to the zero baseline in reverse stagger. Exit: chart frame lifts upward as the 'Datos Bzzoiro' card fades.

prompts.title: Goals for and against — pitch illustration to paired bars
prompts.prompt: Vertical 9:16 frame on charcoal #101412, lower quarter held clear for permanent yellow subtitles. EDITORIAL variant, illustrative football pitch and abstract ball path — no real match events are depicted. A top-down pitch is drawn in 2 px warm white #edf0e6 lines over charcoal, lime #c5ed74 centre circle and centre spot, two goal mouths at the vertical extremes. Two mirrored ball paths loop symmetrically from the centre spot toward each goal and back, warm white ball with a lime motion trail, easing through a smooth curve so the loop reads as pure motion language, never as a scored goal. Spanish labels 'a favor' and 'en contra' sit on slate #8ca6bf plates at the pitch ends; team names 'Liverpool' and 'Brighton' pulse once as the camera performs a slow overhead push. Emphasis: the ball trail brightens for a beat on the shared centre circle, single focal point. Transition: the pitch grid folds vertically into a thin lime seam. Exit: the seam collapses into the statistical card. STATISTICAL variant, paired bars: four horizontal bars, two per team, goals for and goals against, on a shared baseline and one common scale in goles, lime for goals for and slate for goals against, warm white value labels at bar ends, Spanish category labels 'Goles a favor' and 'Goles recibidos' with the unit 'goles' in the axis caption. Values resolve as {{home.gf}} and {{home.ga}} for Liverpool, {{away.gf}} and {{away.ga}} for Brighton. Bars rise from zero in a paired stagger so the for/against contrast inside each team reads first, then a cross-team comparison sweep highlights the largest difference with a warm white bracket and gentle camera push-in. Sample and source treatment: footnote 'muestra' with {{home.n}} and {{away.n}} partidos and source credit Bzzoiro in 22 px slate above the subtitle band. Transition: bars dissolve into a lime particle drift. Exit: values fade, chart frame slides up out of frame.

prompts.title: Clean sheets — defensive energy and shield to count bars
prompts.prompt: Vertical 9:16 layout, charcoal #101412 ground, lower quarter reserved for permanent yellow subtitles and kept free of graphics. EDITORIAL variant, defensive energy with a stylised shield: a single shield silhouette builds centre frame from a lime #c5ed74 outline stroke that draws clockwise, its interior filling with slate #8ca6bf at reduced opacity; a warm white #edf0e6 rim light travels the edge once. The shield then twins, the left one captioned 'Liverpool', the right 'Brighton', both in Spanish on warm white plates below the forms. No numbers, no axes, no sample claims in this variant; tension is carried by motion — the shields rotate slightly toward each other on the beat, sparks of lime dust shed from the rims, and the camera pushes in slowly while the pair settles into a stable hold. One focal point: the seam where the two shield edges nearly touch. Transition: the seam flashes lime and the shields split apart into two vertical halves. Exit: both halves glide off frame edges. STATISTICAL variant, count bars only: two horizontal bars, one per team, on a shared zero baseline with a common scale in partidos, lime for Liverpool and slate for Brighton, warm white value labels at bar ends, Spanish labels 'Arcos en cero' and the axis unit 'partidos'. Counts stay as counts — no conversion into rates or proportions. Values animate as {{home.clean}} for Liverpool and {{away.clean}} for Brighton. Bars grow from the baseline together over roughly 1.2 s, then the larger bar takes emphasis with a soft lime halo and a subtle camera push while the other desaturates slightly. Sample and source treatment: footnote 'muestra' with {{home.n}} and {{away.n}} partidos plus source credit Bzzoiro in 22 px slate just above the subtitle band. Transition: bar fills drain downward into the baseline. Exit: axis ticks fade, chart lifts away upward.

prompts.title: Head-to-head — visual duel to historical count bars
prompts.prompt: Vertical 9:16 stage on charcoal #101412 with the lower quarter permanently reserved for yellow subtitles. EDITORIAL variant, a visual duel: the frame is split by a thin lime #c5ed74 vertical seam, 'Liverpool' in warm white #edf0e6 filling the left field and 'Brighton' filling the right, both Spanish labels set in condensed caps. Two abstract crest blocks — simple geometric marks, no club badges — slide in from the outer edges and collide at the seam on the first beat, producing a diagonal slate #8ca6bf shockwave and a brief lime flare. The seam then breathes, tilting a few degrees left and right with each spoken emphasis, camera performing a slow lateral arc across the duel so parallax separates the two fields. No numerals, axes, sample claims or invented match events in this variant; hierarchy is one focal point at the seam. Transition: the seam widens into a full-frame wipe. Exit: both crest blocks retreat to their edges and dim. STATISTICAL variant, historical grouped count bars: three horizontal bars — victorias Liverpool, victorias Brighton, empates — on a shared zero baseline with one common scale in partidos, lime for Liverpool, slate for Brighton, warm white for draws, warm white value labels at bar ends, Spanish labels 'Victorias Liverpool', 'Victorias Brighton', 'Empates' and axis unit 'partidos'. Values resolve as {{h2h.homeWins}}, {{h2h.awayWins}} and {{h2h.draws}}; the header carries the Spanish note 'Historial, no pronóstico' so the data reads as record, never forecast. Bars grow from zero in sequence, then the leading bar holds emphasis with a lime glow while the camera makes a small push-in. Sample and source treatment: footnote 'muestra' with {{h2h.total}} partidos and source credit Bzzoiro in 22 px slate above the subtitle band. Transition: bars collapse into the baseline and the lime seam reopens. Exit: everything fades to charcoal with the Spanish note last to disappear.
